title: Qwen3.6-27B sole-T16 XTX memory-growth and 8K baseline

protocol.hipengine: Package-default persistent sole-T16 session, token 9707, one discarded warmup plus three measured resets, bulk prefill, BF16 KV, PM4/HIP graph decode, 128 timed transitions, cached compiler artifacts, 5 ms whole-device sysfs VRAM around the complete child process.
protocol.llamacpp_512_4k: Frozen clean same-commit c8e03ce81 packet: standardized llama-bench prefill and 5 ms whole-device peak; context-matched llama-server 128-transition decode.
protocol.llamacpp_8k: Fresh clean same-commit c8e03ce81 standardized llama-bench split-phase 8K/128 row, one warmup and five repetitions, BF16 KV, 5 ms whole-device VRAM. Its decode number is standardized llama-bench at depth 8192, not a context-matched server row.
protocol.memory_scope: Tracked memory is hipEngine allocator/owned-session high water. Whole-device peak delta is sysfs mem_info_vram_used peak minus the pre-process baseline. The cross-engine gate uses whole-device peak delta, never tracked memory.

growth_analysis.conclusion: The apparent growth has two regimes. From 512 through 4K, the dominant avoidable growth is the liveness-aliased bulk-prefill arena and full-sequence hidden buffer, which add 0.541 GiB while BF16 KV adds 0.219 GiB. Above the 4096-row prefill chunk cap, scratch is flat: 0.250 of the 0.258-GiB tracked 4K-to-8K growth is the expected BF16 full-attention KV cache. The fixed 15.280-GiB weight payload is resident footprint, not per-token growth. Whole-device overhead above tracked ownership rises to roughly 0.75 GiB at 4K/8K and needs separate allocator/library attribution.

do_not_repeat: raw-Q4 or raw-plus-T16 sidecars; maximum Q4 residency savings were insufficient and cache-cold performance was rejected
pure or mixed INT8 KV as a default; Qwen3.6-27B quality/capacity promotion remains rejected
any context-specific fallback that changes sole-T16 ownership or regresses current prefill/decode
candidate_constraints.next_profile: Use a narrow cache-only 4K/8K decode profile to rank bytes-per-token/kernel families, while separately attributing the approximately 0.75-GiB whole-device-minus-tracked gap. Select a non-duplicative candidate only after the profile.

decision: Freeze the four-shape baseline and proceed to a narrow 4K/8K decode traffic profile. Do not call the linear 4K-to-8K BF16 KV growth a leak; the actionable short-to-mid-context growth is prefill scratch plus untracked allocator/library overhead. No runtime path changes in this audit.
